output.summary: Perennial water lily native from northern India through China, Korea and Japan to Taiwan and far eastern Russia. Its large, round, puckered leaves, stems and spiny fruits bear sharp prickles, and its violet-and-white flowers often pierce the leaves. The seeds and leaf stalks are eaten; seeds are commonly dried and may be roasted or fried in northern and western India.
output.edibilityNote: Seeds and leaf stalks are eaten; seeds are dried and may be roasted, fried, made into porridge or pudding, or added to soup.
